metas.name: Black Bollard
metas.note: A typical bollard but with a black stripe instead of a red one is commonly found in Wellington, especially in older Generation 3 coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Bright Sandy Cliffs
metas.note:
Bright sandy cliffs are a common sight in the central region of Manawatū-Whanganui. They may also be found in parts of Taranaki, Waikato and a road going into Hawke’s Bay.

NOTE: Sometimes the cliffs may appear like sandy rocks.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Crossbar white paint
metas.note: Some concrete poles in eastern Waikato and Whanganui city have white paint on the middle part of their wooden crossbars. This white painted crossbar can also be found in parts of western Bay of Plenty, Taranaki, Manawatū-Whanganui and eastern Wellington.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Flax Rows
metas.note: While New Zealand flax can be found across the country, if you see them in long neat rows, you should consider Southland.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Gisborne yellow tag
metas.note: A yellow tag, similar in appearance to a cow-tag, is found on most poles in Gisborne. It is also found in a few spots on the South Island, as well as over the border in northern Hawke’s Bay.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Glacial Lakes
metas.note: The area of the Southern Alps, north and south of Queenstown, contains many glacial lakes, which can be recognized by their teal colours and clear waters.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Green Bollard
metas.note: A typical bollard, but with a green stripe, is common in southern Canterbury, as well as in some pockets in eastern Southland.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Hawke's Bay Golden Hills
metas.note: Hawke’s Bay has dry, golden grassy hills, and in Generation 4 it will be sunny with a white Street View car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Holey Poles
metas.note: Holey poles are found most commonly in Southland and around Auckland.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Horizontal Black Sticker
metas.note: A small black horizontal pole sticker, with several numbers, is often found in Taranaki and Wellington. The sticker may rarely be found in parts of Manawatū-Whanganui, Waikato, and southern Hawke's Bay.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Horizontal White Plate
metas.note:
A small white horizontal pole sticker with several numbers is found in several parts of the North Island.

NOTE: The edges of the plate must be straight, meaning they cannot be rounded. Rounded plates are seen all across the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Long Wooden Extensions
metas.note: Long wooden extensions on fences are mainly found in Southland and Hawke’s Bay, but can also be seen in Otago.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Marlborough Pole Guard
metas.note: Most utility poles in the Marlborough region have a long square shaped olive-brown possum guard. These can appear alongside the usual shorter silver possum guards.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Mount Taranaki
metas.note: Mount Taranaki, often referred to as Mount Egmont, is easily distinguished due to its relatively smooth slopes and its pointed, often snowy peak. It can frequently be identified from afar, as the surrounding area is flat.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand Corn
metas.note: Corn is almost exclusively found on the North Island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Solid outer lines without middle line
metas.note:
Solid outer white lines without middle lines are most common in Gisborne, but can also be found in northern Hawke's Bay and Wellington.

NOTE: The roads in Wellington are typically narrower.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Southland Pole Guard
metas.note:
Some poles in Southland feature a long cylindrical silver possum guard.

Sometimes it can look similar to the Marlborough guard, except this is lighter in color(sometimes silver).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Square Concrete Poles
metas.note: Square concrete poles without the usual indent are most common in Southland, but can also be found in Otago, Taranaki and Manawatū-Whanganui.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: State Highway 73
metas.note: State Highway 73, located near Arthur’s Pass, can be recognised by the almost dried out river with an abundance of gravel on the river bed. Additionally, in some frames another google car is visible on the road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Thin Metal Fence Post
metas.note: Fences with thin metal fence posts are almost exclusive to the South island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Tightly Packed Wooden Fences
metas.note: Wooden fences with tightly packed fence posts are most common on the Northern Island and the north of the South Island, as well as on Akaroa.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Timaru Pole Warning
metas.note: Poles near Timaru often have a tall rectangle of orange paint on them with the text “DANGER LIVE WIRES”.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Vertical Black Sticker - 5 digits
metas.note:
A medium sized black vertical sticker with 5 digits is found in West Coast, Tasman, southern Canterbury and southern Northland.

Note that there are similar stickers but they'll be smaller in size.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Vertical Black Sticker - 6 digits with square
metas.note: A long black vertical sticker with 6 digits with a small black square beneath it, is found on most of the North Island, in Southland and in Otago. On the North Island the first digit will be a 3 or a 4, while on the South Island it starts with an 8.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Vineyards
metas.note:
Vineyards are particularly common in the Marlborough and Hawke’s Bay regions.

NOTE: Vineyards can be found throughout New Zealand, so be sure to check other clues as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Waikato Trident Insulator
metas.note:
Poles with the middle insulator being installed on top of a tall metal bar are often found along the Auckland Waikato border, as well as in other parts of Waikato.

Sometimes it can be a metal trident, sometimes it is installed just on a single metal bar extending up.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Warning Sticker
metas.note: A warning sticker attached to poles, which has a yellow danger triangle between two white rectangles, is found in Hawke’s Bay, from lake Taupo to lake Rotorua, in northern Waikato and south of Auckland city.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Wooden fence with big gap
metas.note: Wooden fences with a big gap in-between them are most common on the South island as well as in Taranaki.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.
